root_cause.text: The option walkers in xt_tcpudp.c and xt_dccp.c do not check if the current byte index is the last byte of the option area before reading op[i+1] to determine the next option offset, causing an out-of-bounds read when the final byte is a multi-byte option kind (value >= 2).
root_cause.evidence: The commit message states: "When the last byte of options is a non-single-byte option kind, walkers that advance with i += op[i + 1] ? : 1 can read op[i + 1] past the end of the option area." The patch adds an explicit `i == optlen - 1` check before the dereference in both `tcp_find_option` and `dccp_find_option`.
